script: Good sleep is one of the simplest ways to feel better every day. Most adults need between seven and nine hours each night. Try to go to bed and wake up at the same time, even on weekends, so your body clock stays steady. An hour before bed, dim the lights and put your phone away, because bright screens tell your brain it is still daytime. Keep your bedroom cool, dark and quiet. A cup of coffee in the late afternoon can keep you awake hours later, so switch to water or herbal tea after lunch. If you cannot fall asleep after twenty minutes, get up, read a book in soft light, and go back to bed when you feel sleepy. During the day, spend some time outside in natural light and move your body. Small changes like these, repeated every night, can make your mornings brighter and your days calmer. If you still feel tired after weeks of good habits, talk to a doctor, because poor sleep can have many causes. Rest is not lazy. It is how your body and mind repair themselves.
